text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development plans to invest some $450 million in Romania.
- Dormant commodities exchanges in Romania are still awaiting a new legislation to revive trading, the paper says.
- Romanian companies ask for a devaluation of the national currency in order to stimulate exports, the paper says.
- The Sidex SA steel mill and SNCFR railway authority have each debts amounting to 300 billion lei.
- Opposition parties in parliamwent plan to introduce a motion against the government over what they called a very serious situation in the farming sector.
- Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara is quoted as saying that the government was expected to reach a "compromise" in talks with the IMF's chief negotiatior Poul Thomsen over new credits.
- Rains and a small number of harvesting combines cuts wheat output in several southern counties, the paper says.
- The government decided to turn into "national companies" the regies autonomes grouping mines in the salt and rare metals sectors.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will invest more in Romania's private sector.
- The Romanian Oil Company will retain only two refineries in its new structure, the paper says.
